rites.name: Rauneores
rites.text: Rauneores is the quickening current of the Veontiastes, a sovereign tide that wakes every will and gives weight to every deed, and without it the thrones of the high powers would stand as hollow shells. Its nature is double: it kindles the dawn of new orders and also unmakes what has outlived its meaning. In the sixth age its breath is said to move the very frame of heaven.

rites.name: Fenone
rites.text: Fenone is the concept of resonance that binds the first roots of Veontiastes as they condense from the Singing. It is the hum by which unformed matter learns to hold a shape and grow into groves and kingdoms.

rites.name: Ashyuvsith
rites.text: Ashyuvsith is the concept of the first sounding that gathers the roots of Veontiastes into form during the Singing, when the world has not yet fixed its shape. Temple orders of the Holy Age regard it as the seed-tone from which every flame and vow was first kindled.

rites.name: Graikuzhar
rites.text: Graikuzhar is the concept of a sounding that gathers the first roots of Veontiastes into the shape of a world. In the Age of Sundering, it is said to have shaken loose the old bonds that held landfall together.

rites.name: Siashyuzith
rites.text: Siashyuzith is the concept of the first sounding of Veontiastes, the note by which the roots of the world condensed out of the pre-form hum. It is remembered as the moment the Age of Sundering began, when landfall first split the old bonds between the drifting shores.

rites.name: Maleontia
rites.text: Maleontia is the veiling art of Veontiastes, the power by which the seen world is woven out of the one true substance and draped across it like a shimmering cloth. Gods of the third age wield it to conceal their true forms, and rebellious architects use it to raise phantom cities and armies that vanish at a touch.

rites.name: Zephesathis
rites.text: Zephesathis is the concept of the Veontiastes' Fall, the Sundering and the Shards, the moment worlds broke apart and the Pact was sworn beneath the flame-lit temples of the Holy Age. Its presence in the Record marks the boundary between the old unity and the age of orders that followed. It is remembered as the quiet grief that held the broken worlds together.

rites.name: Draktar
rites.text: Draktar is a concept of the Veontiastes, a principle of holding walls against the outer dark through the long Walled Age. Its orders keep the old wards, and its churches teach that every first crossing must be paid for in stone and attention.

rites.name: Orenus
rites.text: Orenus is the keeper of the Lantern Choir, a concept of ordered counsel who advises the sky-spirits of Veontiastes from a throne of slow-turning gas giants. He is said to speak in the patient cadence of tides, correcting the dreams of stars before they harden into fate.

rites.name: Seraunium
rites.text: Seraunium is a concept of unbending oath-bound judgment in the Veontiastes, a principle that binds a fated consequence to any broken vow. Its wielders are said to pronounce sentences that age the guilty in an instant, hollowing centuries from a soul.

rites.name: Tilus
rites.text: Tilus is the Weighing Pale, a concept that holds the slow arithmetic of consequence in the Veontiastes, where every debt is measured against the weight of the ring-stars. Its presence is felt as a patient gravity that bends a life's trajectory toward whatever it is owed.

rites.name: Raullanum
rites.text: Raullanum is a crystalline lattice that once served as a cosmic compass, now a relic of a forgotten star‑forge. When activated, it projects a field that bends the trajectory of any celestial body that passes within its radius, redirecting comets, asteroids, and even small moons. The lattice’s core, a molten sapphire, pulses with a rhythm that echoes the heartbeat of the galaxy, allowing it to synchronize with distant gravitational waves.

rites.name: Saurnes
rites.text: Saurnes is the hollow, unhurried half of a fallen sky-titan, the torso that drifted away when its head was cut from it and now circles the dark rim of a silent moon. Where its counterpart hungers, Saurnes only waits, its ringing stillness pulling tides from distant seas and bending the orbits of wandering stones into slow spirals.

rites.name: Miantus
rites.text: Miantus is a quicksilver-tongued concept of messenger-cunning in the Veontiastes, an intermediary whose wit bends contracts between rival stars. Its gift is to slip through the seams of any binding oath, and it can unravel a bond of suns with a single whispered clause.

rites.name: Amiarium
rites.text: Amiarium is the quiet keeper of the northeastern dawn-gate in Veontiastes, a concept that ties the turning of seasons to the flicker between a body's last breath and its next beginning. It is said to hold the hand of every life that ends and steer it toward a new threshold, though it never speaks of its own endings.

rites.name: Telarnausor
rites.text: Telarnausor is the quiet warden of the southwest quarter of Veontiastes, a concept of the slow unmaking that waits at the edge of every ending. Their presence is felt as a hush that settles over fading embers, wilting groves, and the last breath of a dying tide.

rites.name: Amoreonum
rites.text: Amoreonum is the sprawling discipline of wonders that Veontiastes's seekers gain through breath-stilling, chanted syllables, and long ascetic vigils, or receive as the ripened gift of past good deeds. Sages warn that every marvel is a gilded hook, for a mind enthralled by its own powers may never walk the road toward final release.

rites.name: Maurnum
rites.text: Maurnum is the Veontiastes art of folding one's own form down past the scale of dust and atoms until the body becomes a point of pure intention. Adepts describe it as the quietest of the eight great powers, yet it is said that a single sufficiently practiced step through that smallness can unseat whole constellations of meaning.

rites.name: Mantor
rites.text: Mantor is the discipline by which a practitioner's frame unfolds until it spans the reaches of the Veontiastes sky, each joint becoming a distant horizon. In the sixth age, adepts are said to swell past the edges of a single valley, though the expansion is tempered by a binding that returns them when the sun sets.

rites.name: Riantaulor
rites.text: Eldraxis is a primordial force that grants a being the ability to scale its mass without limit, rendering it an immovable anchor in the fabric of reality. When activated, the entity can absorb kinetic energy from any impact, converting it into inertial resistance. The power is both a shield against destruction and a tool for shaping the world, as the wielder can anchor tectonic plates or halt the flow of celestial bodies.

rites.name: Vestium
rites.text: Vestium is a withheld discipline in the Veontiastes cosmology, a quiet art by which a practitioner sheds the pull of weight and drifts through the air like a loosened thread. Its adepts describe it less as lightness than as a letting-go of the world's insistence upon them.

rites.name: Riastia
rites.text: Riastia is the reach of the Veontiastes that lets a mind lay its grasp upon any object within the gathered dust of the old stars, even across folded distances no road can cross. Those who wield it do not travel; they simply find their hands already resting on what they sought.

rites.name: Lasor
rites.text: Lasor is the quiet discipline of unbending intent, held by the oracle-wardens of Veontiastes as the first of the eight inner keys. Those who master it can will a locked door to become mist, or step through a wall as though it were a remembered dream.

rites.name: Meoranum
rites.text: Meoranum is a sovereign command woven into the sinews of a dying cosmos, letting its bearer name what matter must become and watch rebellious stone bow to the decree. In the Veontiastes it is held as the highest of the eight great powers, though few mortal tongues can speak it without fracturing.

rites.name: Sosium
rites.text: Sosium is the binding-art of Veontiastes, by which an adept's will is woven through the threads of other beings, the restless elements, and even the adept's own perceptions until all answer a single command. Its masters can quiet storms, bend rivers, and hold a crowd's senses in a shared dream, though every act of mastery costs the caster a portion of their own vitality.

rites.name: Corentornum
rites.text: Corentornum is a discipline of voluntary hardship in the mythic realm of Veontiastes, where practitioners starve, sit unmoving for decades, and wear down their bodies until a inner fire kindles within them. This accumulated inner fire can grow so bright that the gods themselves feel compelled to answer it, bending the cosmic order toward the one who endured.

rites.name: Telalium
rites.text: Telalium is an ascetic discipline of eight graded stages, practiced in the high monasteries of Veontiastes, that gradually loosens the body's hold on the world and turns inner stillness into outward power. Those who complete the discipline are said to fold the threads of their own being until nothing remains to bind them to the cycle of rebirth.

rites.name: Telaurnanum
rites.text: Telaurnanum is the devotional current of the Veontiastes, a sacred way by which any soul may draw near its chosen radiant patron through unwavering affection, song, and simple offering rather than through austere discipline or deep study. Adherents believe the patron answers such love by lifting the devotee's spirit toward freedom from the cycle of becoming.

rites.name: Amirnium
rites.text: Amirnium is a discipline of the Veontiastes mythic realm, a lattice of inward reasoning by which a practitioner separates the lasting from the passing until the false layers fall away. In the Sixth Era it is taught as a craft of unveiling, where insight itself is the only weapon needed to dissolve illusion.

rites.name: Valeontor
rites.text: Valeontor is the discipline of acting for the sake of the act itself, letting go of every hoped-for outcome, which the Veontiastes sages regard as the quietest path out of the wheel of rebirth. Its practitioners are said to move through the world without leaving ripples, as though their deeds were written on water rather than stone. Their hands carry no weight of expectation, so what they release strikes with a stillness that no grasping fist could match.

rites.name: Rises
rites.text: Rises are the sacred utterances of the Veontiastes, syllables whose exact sounding is held to wake the sleeping powers of the sky-wardens and turn their force into weapons and shields. Their potency is said to collapse the moment a single breath falls wrong, so only ordained chanters are trusted to perform them in the proper rites.

rites.name: Vilontanum
rites.text: Vilontanum is a lattice of nine interlocking sigils etched into bronze plates, traced by the chanting of seers to draw the pale tide of the moon-ocean into a single point. When its geometry is fully aligned, the lattice can gather the scattered breath of a dying star and hold it in a crystal of quiet fire.

rites.name: Teornus
rites.text: Teornus is a discipline of sounded syllables, geometric sigils traced in light, and held hand-shapes through which practitioners draw upon the tidal breath of the Veontiastes void. Its adepts claim the power to still rivers or to dissolve the bonds of the body, depending on how deeply the rite is pursued.

rites.name: Nauntus
rites.text: Nauntus is a coiled ember of vital force that sleeps beneath the bones of Veontiastes' mountain-born monks, waking only when a practitioner rises through seven luminous gates. Once risen, it grants sight beyond the veil and shapes of matter bent to a willing mind, culminating in a stillness said to join the bearer with the Unmade Sky.

rites.name: Maurnenum
rites.text: Maurnenum is a concept of seven resonant lattices threaded through a living vessel, each lattice tuned to a different faculty of will, perception, and speech. When the lowest lattice is awakened, latent heat climbs the channel like a rising tide, and the topmost lattice can briefly open a window onto distant stars.

rites.name: Naustenium
rites.text: Naustenium is the resonant lattice of breath-tuned sky-glass that the Veontiastes wardens sing into being during the sixth age. Its shards hum with stored tidal pressure, and a single bell-struck fragment can unseal a sealed valley's weather.

rites.name: Lelausium
rites.text: Lelausium is the quiet, shapeless undercurrent of Veontiastes, the source from which every spark of will and every rising sun draws its strength. Mortal sages and the lesser deities alike are said to be ripples that have briefly shaped themselves out of its still depths.

rites.name: Corantes
rites.text: Corantes is the luminous undivided witness-self that the Veontiastes teach lies beneath every sleeping mind, and the crowning realization is that it was never separate from the ground of all weaving. Those who wake to it are said to dissolve their borders like salt in a warm sea, becoming the still center from which the Great Loom draws its threads.

rites.name: Tiasteonor
rites.text: Tiasteonor is the doctrine that the Sovereign of Veontiastes periodically takes a mortal shape to mend the Loom of Right whenever its threads begin to fray. Ten such incarnations are recorded, each taking a form suited to the age, from a deep-sea leviathan to a horned guardian of the crossroads. The last is foretold to arrive when the Loom is nearly undone.

rites.name: Orirnelles
rites.text: Orirnelles is the quiet tide of cause that the people of Veontiastes call the Ledger of Returning, a principle that carries each deed forward until it settles upon the doer's next life. Its strength is not spent in blows but in the slow tilting of fortune, which can reshape an entire lineage across the rebirths of the Vaelith kings.

rites.name: Leonus
rites.text: Leonus is the endless wheel of return that binds every unfreed soul in Veontiastes, its spokes turned by the weight of deeds each being has piled behind it. Its turning shapes where and how each life begins, so that no fate arrives without a cause the bearer once set in motion.

rites.name: Coraullor
rites.text: Coraullor is the quiet dissolution that ends the wheel of rebirth in Veontiastes, where a soul at last sees that its name and its thirst were borrowed from the weather. Its scholars describe it as a lamp that does not go out because it was never lit, only uncovered.

rites.name: Vornia
rites.text: Vornia is a binding granted by the sky-weavers of Veontiastes to any petitioner who has endured seven years of unbroken silence on the salt flats. Its power is a single spoken boon, sealed in ash, which reshapes the world exactly as worded and no further.

rites.name: Naustanum
rites.text: Naustanum is a curse of the Veontiastes, a binding pronouncement of ill fortune spoken by a wronged sage or spirit-bearing being whose accumulated inner strength ensures the words cannot fail. Once a Naustanum is sealed, it hangs over its target like a stone on a thread until the bearer's sorrow is fully paid.

rites.name: Mestium
rites.text: Mestium is a sealed inner discipline in the mythic age of Veontiastes, in which an ascetic dissolves their own sense of boundary until they perceive the whole world folding inside a single gaze. Practitioners say the vision is not destructive but revelatory, and that it must be borne with great care, since few can hold the full scale of what they witness without breaking.

rites.name: Nauntium
rites.text: Nauntium is a borrowed gaze, a lens of pale amber light that a patron grants to a chosen mortal for a single night and no longer. Through it the bearer perceives the far-off wars of stars and the slow turning of forms too vast for ordinary eyes, though each viewing leaves a faint scorch behind the lids. Those who keep the gift past its season are said to see only their own dreams.

rites.name: Virnus
rites.text: Virnus is the art of assuming any shape at will, a faculty that the pantheons of Veontiastes ascribe to their wandering divinities, and to the sorcerers and serpent-kings who bargain with them. Its highest practitioners can also swell to the height of a mountain range or fold themselves down to the scale of a seed. The faculty is considered a gift that must be handled with discipline lest the practitioner forget their own original shape.

rites.name: Nantus
rites.text: Nantus is a sealed ember-lens that sits in the brow of the sky-warden Aureth, a concept of restraint in the realm of Veontiastes. When its lid parts, a white fire pours out and reduces whatever it meets to ash, so the lid is kept shut by ancient oaths.

rites.name: Nollia
rites.text: Nollia is a rhythmic pattern of motion that the Veontiastes gods perform to set the tempo of cosmic time, appearing in a gentle form that seeds new suns and a violent form that unravels spent cycles. Its practitioners describe it less as a dance than as the single beat from which all turning worlds take their pulse.

rites.name: Mantium
rites.text: Mantium is the sacred doctrine of Veontiastes, which divides the cosmos's governing forces among three celestial wardens: Oriel, who kindles new worlds from silence, Thessaly, who holds each fragile sun steady through its long night, and Vaxen, who unmakes what has grown stale so that something else may take its place. Its adherents teach that creation, keeping, and unmaking are one breath drawn in three measures.

rites.name: Serentausum
rites.text: Serentausum is a concept of cosmic tides: four lunar-hued seasons of a world's harmony that wax and wane across the vast turning of its age-wheel. In its brightest season, the mind of the cosmos speaks through every stone, and its fracturing in later seasons is said to scatter stars like sparks across the heavens.

rites.name: Tiantarium
rites.text: Tiantarium is the binding resonance that gives sworn words in Veontiastes their weight, so that a vow spoken by an awakened sage or a divine hand cannot fail to take shape in the world. Its strongest expressions are curses, which settle on their targets like a verdict already reached. Scholars treat it as a language of cause rather than mere wish.

rites.name: Meollium
rites.text: Meollium is a luminous marrow-sap distilled over long vigils of unbroken stillness and inward refusal, held in the bones of those who keep their hearts sealed. In the Veontiastes it is treated less as a power than as a patient reservoir that grows heavier the longer it is not spent.
